text:
Dubai residential activity accelerated in the final week of October, with 11,608 registered sales totaling AED 34.33bn. This volume represents an 11.4 percent increase compared to the previous four weeks, which recorded 10,419 sales and AED 27.34bn in value. Mortgage registrations also rose to 4,630, up from 3,890 in the prior period, indicating a parallel expansion in financing activity alongside direct transfers.

Median residential pricing reached AED 1,688 per square foot, a 0.8 percent rise from the previous four-week median of AED 1,675. The off-plan share of sales decreased to 57.2 percent from 65.4 percent, suggesting a shift in transaction mix toward completed properties. Top performing areas by volume include Dubai South with 3,669 sales and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,285 sales over the last twelve weeks.

The rental market processed 91,552 Ejari contracts, with renewals accounting for 51.3 percent of the total. The median residential rent stands at AED 69,750 per year. Estimated gross yields remain strongest in Zaabeel First at 8.9 percent and International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent, both for flats. In contrast, premium areas like Business Bay show a 5.4 percent decline in median price per square foot over twelve weeks.

Investors should monitor Al Yufrah 1, which saw a 43.3 percent increase in median price per square foot over twelve weeks, and Dubai Industrial City with a 12.8 percent rise. Cooling trends are evident in Liwan and Palm Deira, both down over 13 percent. Anomaly detection flagged 1,049 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from comparable medians. These figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
